Empirical Research Plan – Ownership, Regulation and Bank Risk (1996–2001 panel of 296 large banks in 48 countries)  

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Main strategy: Difference-in-Differences with staggered adoption (“event-study/DiD hybrid”) embedded in a triple-difference framework.

Why this is appropriate  
• National regulatory rules (deposit-insurance introduction/upgrade, higher minimum capital-to-risk-weighted-assets ratios, new activity restrictions) changed in different years across countries between 1996 and 2001.  
• Bank-level ownership structure is fixed or changes slowly and is highly heterogeneous within each country.  
• We can therefore compare changes in risk at (i) banks headquartered in countries that tighten a given rule vs. banks in countries that do not (first difference), (ii) before vs. after the rule change (second difference), and (iii) between banks with high vs. low shareholder power (third difference).  

Econometric specification (conceptually)  

Risk_{bct} = α_b + γ_ct + β₁(Reg_{ct}) + β₂(OwnPower_{bc})  
               + β₃(Reg_{ct} × OwnPower_{bc}) + X′_{bct}δ + ε_{bct}

α_b = bank FE; γ_ct = country-year FE (absorbs all national macro & regulatory shocks).  
β₃ captures whether the regulatory effect on risk is amplified or muted when shareholders are powerful.

Event-study leads/lags of Reg_{ct} test the parallel-trend assumption; stacked-DiD estimator (Sun & Abraham, 2021) removes bias from staggered timing.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
Reg_{ct}. One rule handled at a time. Example: explicit deposit-insurance adoption dummy that switches from 0 to 1 in the implementation year and stays 1 thereafter. (Alternative rules: stricter capital-requirement tier-1 ratio; new activity restriction index.)

Shareholder-power variable  
OwnPower_{bc}. = 1 if largest shareholder holds ≥25 % of voting rights OR if the bank belongs to a pyramidal group with ultimate owner voting rights ≥25 %. 0 otherwise (widely-held benchmark). Time-invariant average over 1996-2001 (or updated when stakes jump ±10 ppts).

Control group / counterfactual  
• Banks in countries that have not (yet) implemented the regulatory change during the sample window.  
• Within treated countries: banks observed before adoption.

Treatment timing  
Country-specific adoption years from Barth-Caprio-Levine (2006) updates; e.g., Korea upgrades deposit insurance in 1997, Brazil in 1998, etc.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends: Absent the regulatory change, risk at banks in adopting and non-adopting countries would have followed similar trends, conditional on bank and country-year FE.  
Plausibility: Large-bank sample, common Basel-I environment, ability to inspect pre-trend graphs and formal pre-trend tests.

A2. No anticipatory behavior: Banks do not change risk materially before the formal adoption year after controlling for leads.  
Plausibility: Dates are legal implementation rather than announcement; still test with leads.

A3. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA): Regulation of country c does not directly affect risk of banks in country c′≠c (no cross-border depositor spillovers).  
Plausibility: Reasonable but international banks exist; robustness drops multinational banks whose main assets lie abroad.

A4. Ownership structure exogenous to timing of regulatory change: controlling stakes are not rearranged precisely in anticipation of regulation.  
Plausibility: Stakes move slowly; check by regressing changes in stakes on upcoming regulation leads.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Remedies
--------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Endogenous policy adoption (countries adopt insurance after banking crises).  
Fix: Country-specific linear trends, include Crisis_{ct} controls, and do an instrumental-variable-DiD where adoption is instrumented with IMF-program conditionality dummies.

T2. Concurrent shocks (Asian crisis 1997–98) that correlate with both regulation and risk.  
Fix: Country-year FE already absorb those; additionally interact crisis dummies with region to allow heterogeneous crisis effects.

T3. Ownership may itself change after the shock (reverse causality).  
Fix: Freeze OwnPower at pre-treatment level; drop banks that change control (M&A) within ±2 years of adoption; run robustness with lagged ownership.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
--------------------------------------------------------------------


```r
# --------------- 1. Load libraries ---------------
library(data.table)
library(fixest)         # fast high-dim panel regressions
library(did)            # Sun & Abraham estimators
library(ggplot2)

# --------------- 2. Load and merge data ----------
banks   <- fread("bank_panel_1996_2001.csv")      # accounting & returns
owners  <- fread("bank_ownership.csv")            # voting rights etc.
reg     <- fread("country_reg_rules.csv")         # regulation by cty-year
laws    <- fread("shareholder_protection.csv")    # La Porta et al.

data <- merge(banks, owners,  by = c("bank_id","year"), all.x = TRUE)
data <- merge(data,  reg,    by = c("country","year"), all.x = TRUE)
data <- merge(data,  laws,   by = c("country","year"), all.x = TRUE)

# --------------- 3. Variable construction --------
data[, own_power := fifelse(vote_rights_largest >= .25, 1, 0)]
data[, explicit_DI := explicit_DI_indicator]     # deposit insurance dummy

# Event-time relative to adoption
data[, DI_year := min(year[explicit_DI==1]), by = country]
data[, rel_time := year - DI_year]              # leads/lags
# Trim to [-4,4] window for event-study
data <- data[rel_time >= -4 & rel_time <= 4]

# Main risk measure
data[, zscore := (roa + equity_asset_ratio)/sd_roa_3yr]

# --------------- 4. Main DiD regression ----------
spec_main <- feols(
  zscore ~ explicit_DI * own_power + bank_controls + 
            shareholder_protection + gdp_pc +
            bank_controls:year | bank_id + country_year,
  cluster = ~ country,
  data = data
)

summary(spec_main)

# --------------- 5. Sun & Abraham ATT -----------
sa_fit <- att_gt(yname = "zscore",
                 tname = "year",
                 idname = "bank_id",
                 gname = "DI_year",            # cohort = adoption year
                 xformla = ~ own_power + bank_controls,
                 data = data)
agg_effects <- aggte(sa_fit, type = "dynamic")
ggdid(agg_effects)

# --------------- 6. Robustness: drop multinationals
robust <- feols(
  zscore ~ explicit_DI * own_power | bank_id + country_year,
  cluster = ~ country,
  data = data[num_foreign_subsidiaries < 3]      # proxy for multinational
)
summary(robust)
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Theory suggests diversified shareholders value upside and limited downside, so when shareholders are powerful, deposit insurance (which further subsidizes downside risk) should raise risk more strongly. Hence:

β₁ (effect of deposit insurance with weak shareholders) – may be small or mildly positive.  
β₃ (interaction) – positive: explicit deposit insurance increases z-score volatility or lowers z-score by ~10-15 % of within-bank SD when owners hold ≥25 % voting rights.

Under stronger shareholder-protection laws the disciplining role of minority investors rises, counteracting block-holder risk appetite; thus the marginal effect of concentrated ownership on risk should be muted in high-protection jurisdictions.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DiD)  
(C1–C5 adopted from Cunningham 2021)

C1: Parallel pre-trends visually & statistically (1)  
C2: No anticipation / lead coefficients ≈ 0 (1)  
C3: No simultaneous treatments that differentially hit treated vs. control (0.5)  
C4: Stable composition – no selective entry/exit (0.5)  
C5: SUTVA / no interference across countries (0.5)  

Total ≈ 3.5 / 5 – credible but not iron-clad; robustness checks essential.
